messages:
maria chen: quick check — thinking about adding an explicit early-ack escape hatch for the continuous batcher. hit a tail case where a runaway tenant starves tiny low-latency reqs.
jon park: +1, can you sketch what the hatch does? drop to dedicated tiny fastpath or just ack early and push to a separate queue?
samir patel: my brain: early-ack -> caller gets response that we queued the request (optimistic), then background requeue to slow coalesce. risky for correctness unless we mark idempotency.
kevin li: we should avoid changing app-visible semantics. prefer a short-circuit fastpath: small-size requests get fenced to a tiny-window queue with strict headroom. no early-ack.
maria chen: agreed on avoiding app changes. problem is the tiny-window queue still gets backpressured when a tenant floods. we need queue-fencing + per-tenant soft caps.
jon park: proposal: when tenant rate > X, mark their batches as "fenced" and move new tiny requests into a protected per-tenant microqueue with token budget. this microqueue can be configured to evict oldest/inflight if exceeding headroom.
samir patel: evicting oldest could break some streaming callers. maybe evict lowest-priority or non-streaming first. also need clear telemetry so we can tune X.
kevin li: agreed, add priority bit to request envelope: streaming:true/false, priority:0-3. default 1. scheduler uses priority to evict low-prio first.
ops-bot: deploy-batcher-refactor v2.3 deployed to staging — perf tests queued. :rocket:
maria chen: another angle — kv-cache warmup causes long tails after fence flips. if we move a tenant to microqueue, their kv cache misses spike and latency worsens. we should pre-warm expected kv keys on fence transition.
jon park: pre-warm strategy: when we detect a fence event, trigger async warmup job that replays last N prefixes for that tenant into KV cache. cheap if we cap N, maybe 10. can we rely on cached embeddings?
samir patel: 10 sounds fine. we need a safe replay mechanism: do not re-execute user-visible side effects. replay must be read-only to model runtime.
kevin li: implement warmup as internal shadow requests with tag `warmup=true`. runtime will skip billing and side-effect hooks. small rate limit so it doesn't add pressure.
maria chen: good. action items: (1) add microqueue + per-tenant token budget (2) add priority bit to envelope (3) add warmup job on fence transition (4) telemetry: fence events, microqueue evictions, warmup success rate.
jon park: timeline? can we get a spike-protection PoC in 1 week?
samir patel: I can prototype microqueue and priority logic this week. will mock warmup with a simple replay loop.
kevin li: I'll add envelope changes and operator knobs (X threshold, microqueue size, warmup N).
maria chen: svc owner signoff: I'll run an SLO impact simulation once we have PoC. also add a runtime feature flag `microqueue-experiment` so we can toggle per-AZ.
jon park: sounds good. one more thought — we should surface a fallback policy: if microqueue is overwhelmed for >T seconds, route to a cheaper model variant rather than drop. less cost but up.
samir patel: fallback to cheaper model needs compatibility checks. but we do have model variants table; we can wire a mapping by tenant tier.
kevin li: will add fallback mapping but keep it off by default.
maria chen: thanks all. putting notes in RFC follow-up doc and will post a short summary to #eng-runtime.
jon park: :thumbsup:
ops-bot: perf-test results: staging batcher load test shows 12% lower p99 with microqueue disabled, 28% lower p99 with warmup stub — more once PoC lands.
maria chen: great, keep updates here.
